23259-home-taxidermy-for-pleasure-and-pr.title: or office decoration
23259-home-taxidermy-for-pleasure-and-pr.creator: ALBERT B. FARNHAM, Taxidermist
23259-home-taxidermy-for-pleasure-and-pr.description: A book by ALBERT B. FARNHAM, Taxidermist. This volume of the Pleasure and Profit Library is offered to the hunter, trapper, fisher, vacationist and out of doors people in general. In the study and practice of taxidermy for several years I have failed to find any work written primarily for these every day nature lovers, though they probably handle a greater number of interesting specimens of animal life than all other classes of people.

27463-the-wonders-of-the-jungle-book-two.title: The Wonders Of The Jungle Book Two
27463-the-wonders-of-the-jungle-book-two.creator: Unknown
27463-the-wonders-of-the-jungle-book-two.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. THE ELEPHANT HERD A REPUBLIC 1  The Duties of the President 2  He Must Provide Daily Food 3  He Must Provide Daily Drink 9  He Must Keep Order in the Herd 12  He Must Avoid Danger from Outside 18

65053-meet-me-in-tomorrow.title: Meet Me In Tomorrow
65053-meet-me-in-tomorrow.creator: Unknown
65053-meet-me-in-tomorrow.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. She wrinkled her nose at him. "I think you're a beast, too. But as for Andy, he takes first prize. He had to go and ruin the date I made for him and Susie. It practically broke her heart that she wasn't going with us today."

arxiv-2111-13306.title: Compatible L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebras
arxiv-2111-13306.creator: Apurba Das
arxiv-2111-13306.description: Abstract A compatible L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebra is a graded vector space together with two compatible L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebra structures on it. Given a graded vector space, we construct a graded Lie algebra whose Maurer-Cartan elements are precisely compatible L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebra structures on it.

arxiv-2206-13107.title: Observation of critical phase transition in a generalized Aubry-André-Harper model on a superconducting quantum processor with tunable couplers
arxiv-2206-13107.creator: Hao Li, Yong-Yi Wang, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Xiaohui Song, Gui-Han Liang, Zheng-Yang Mei, Bozhen Zhou, He Zhang, Jia-Chi Zhang, Shu Chen, Shiping Zhao, Ye Tian, Zhan-Ying Yang, Zhongcheng Xiang, Kai Xu, Dongning Zheng, Heng Fan
arxiv-2206-13107.description: Abstract Quantum simulation enables study of many-body systems in non-equilibrium by mapping to a controllable quantum system, providing a new tool for computational intractable problems. Here, using a programmable quantum processor with a chain of 10 superconducting qubits interacted through tunable couplers, we simulate the one-dimensional generalized Aubry-André-Harper model for three different phases, i.e., extended, localized and critical phases.

arxiv-2207-07217.title: Modeling of radiative emission from shallow color centers in single crystalline diamond
arxiv-2207-07217.creator: Maryam Zahedian 1,∗ , Jietian Liu 1,∗ , Ricardo Vidrio 1 , Shimon Kolkowitz 2 , Jennifer T. Choy 1,∗∗
arxiv-2207-07217.description: Abstract Optically active defects in diamond are widely used as bright single-photon sources for quantum sensing, computing, and communication. For many applications, it is useful to place the emitter close to the diamond surface, where the radiative properties of the emitter are strongly modified by its dielectric environment.

arxiv-2212-03075.title: Systematic Assessment of Fuzzers using Mutation Analysis
arxiv-2212-03075.creator: Philipp Görz, Björn Mathis, Keno Hassler, Emre Güler, Thorsten Holz, Andreas Zeller, Rahul Gopinath
arxiv-2212-03075.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Philipp Görz, Björn Mathis, Keno Hassler, Emre Güler, Thorsten Holz, Andreas Zeller, Rahul Gopinath. Fuzzing is an important method to discover vulnerabilities in programs. Despite considerable progress in this area in the past years, measuring and comparing the effectiveness of fuzzers is still an open research question.

arxiv-2212-11902.title: Classical gases with singular densities
arxiv-2212-11902.creator: Luca Di Persio, Yuri Kondratiev, Viktorya Vardanyan
arxiv-2212-11902.description: Abstract We study classical continuous systems with singular distributions of velocities. Radon measures with the infinite mass give these distributions. Positions of particles in such systems are no longer usual configurations in the location space, leading to the necessity of developing new analytical tools to study considered models. Keywords: Classical gases; Poisson point process; Correlation functions; Discrete measures 2010 MSC.

arxiv-2307-14421.title: On the likelihoods of finding very metal-poor (and old) stars in the Milky Way’s disc, bulge, and halo On the likelihoods of finding very metal-poor (and old) stars in the Milky Way’s disc, bulge, and halo – References
arxiv-2307-14421.creator: Diego Sotillo-Ramos, Maria Bergemann, Jennifer K.S. Friske, Annalisa Pillepich
arxiv-2307-14421.description: Abstract Recent observational studies have uncovered a small number of very metal-poor stars with cold kinematics in the Galactic disc and bulge. However, their origins remain enigmatic. We select a total of 138 Milky Way (MW) analogs from the TNG50 cosmological simulation based on their z = 0 z=0 properties: disky morphology, stellar mass, and local environment.

arxiv-2401-06027.title: Examining Kempe equivalence via commutative algebra
arxiv-2401-06027.creator: Hidefumi Ohsugi and Akiyoshi Tsuchiya
arxiv-2401-06027.description: Abstract . Kempe equivalence is a classical and important notion on vertex coloring in graph theory. In the present paper, we introduce several ideals associated with graphs and provide a method to determine whether two k k -colorings are Kempe equivalent via commutative algebra.

arxiv-2401-07671.title: CLSA-CIM: A C ross- L ayer S cheduling A pproach for C omputing- i n- M emory Architectures This work was funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF, Germany) in the project NeuroSys (Project Nos. 03ZU1106CA).
arxiv-2401-07671.creator: Rebecca Pelke , Jose Cubero-Cascante , Nils Bosbach , Felix Staudigl , Rainer Leupers , Jan Moritz Joseph
arxiv-2401-07671.description: Abstract The demand for efficient ml ( ml ) accelerators is growing rapidly, driving the development of novel computing concepts such as rram ( rram )-based tiled cim ( cim ) architectures. cim allows to compute within the memory unit, resulting in faster data processing and reduced power consumption.

arxiv-2402-07302.title: A Review of the GIC Blocker Placement Problem
arxiv-2402-07302.creator: Arthur K. Barnes, Adam Mate, Russell Bent
arxiv-2402-07302.description: Abstract Space weather poses a tremendous threat to power systems: geomagnetic disturbances could result in widespread disruptions and long-duration blackouts, including severe damage to system components. To mitigate their impacts, a handful of strategies exist, with the most promising being the deployment of transformer neutral blocking devices.

arxiv-2403-00272.title: Dual Pose-invariant Embeddings: Learning Category and Object-specific Discriminative Representations for Recognition and Retrieval
arxiv-2403-00272.creator: Rohan Sarkar, Avinash Kak
arxiv-2403-00272.description: Abstract In the context of pose-invariant object recognition and retrieval, we demonstrate that it is possible to achieve significant improvements in performance if both the category-based and the object-identity-based embeddings are learned simultaneously during training. In hindsight, that sounds intuitive because learning about the categories is more fundamental than learning about the individual objects that correspond to those categories.

arxiv-2406-00831.title: Percolation games on rooted, edge-weighted random trees
arxiv-2406-00831.creator: Sayar Karmakar, Moumanti Podder, Souvik Roy, Soumyarup Sadhukhan
arxiv-2406-00831.description: Abstract . Consider a rooted Galton-Watson tree T T , to each of whose edges we assign, independently, a weight that equals + 1 +1 with probability p 1 p_{1} , 0 0 with probability p 0 p_{0} and − 1 -1 with probability p − 1 = 1 − p 1 − p 0 p_{-1}=1-p_{1}-p_{0} .

arxiv-2503-10845.title: Panopticon: Advancing Any-Sensor Foundation Models for Earth Observation
arxiv-2503-10845.creator: Leonard Waldmann, Ando Shah, Yi Wang, Nils Lehmann, Adam J. Stewart, Zhitong Xiong, Xiao Xiang Zhu, Stefan Bauer, John Chuang
arxiv-2503-10845.description: Abstract Earth observation (EO) data features diverse sensing platforms with varying spectral bands, spatial resolutions, and sensing modalities. While most prior work has constrained inputs to fixed sensors, a new class of any-sensor foundation models able to process arbitrary sensors has recently emerged.

arxiv-2511-08092.title: Pruning as Regularization: Sensitivity-Aware One-Shot Pruning in ASR
arxiv-2511-08092.creator: Julian Irigoyen, Arthur Söhler, Andreas Søeborg Kirkedal
arxiv-2511-08092.description: Abstract We challenge the conventional view of neural network pruning as solely a compression technique, demonstrating that one-shot magnitude pruning serves as a powerful implicit regularizer for ASR. Using Whisper-small, we combine gradient- and Fisher-based sensitivity diagnostics with targeted, component-wise pruning.

arxiv-2602-09096.title: A Faint Progenitor System for the Faint Supernova 2024vjm
arxiv-2602-09096.creator: Erez A. Zimmerman, Avishay Gal-Yam, Paul J. Groot, Eran O. Ofek, Jan van Roestel, Andrea Pastorello, Stefano Valenti, Aravind P. Ravi, Ping Chen, Steve Schulze, Nadejda Blagorodnova, Maxime Wavasseur, Marco A. Gómez-Muñoz, Hugo Tranin, Simon de Wet, Giorgos Leloudas, Paul M. Vreeswijk, Lindsey A. Kw
arxiv-2602-09096.description: Abstract Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) are well known for their role as standardizable cosmological candles. Their uniformity is credited to their single origin as thermonuclear explosions of White dwarf (WD) stars (e.g., 77 ; 48 ). Nevertheless, some SNe Ia break this regularity.

arxiv-2604-06536.creator: Md Umar Hashmi 1 , Harsha Nagarajan 2 , Dirk Van Hertem 1

arxiv-2604-15598.title: When do trajectories matter? Identifiability analysis for stochastic transport phenomena
arxiv-2604-15598.creator: Matthew J. Simpson, Michael J. Plank

arxiv-2606-22419.title: Knowledge-Graph Grounding Helps LLMs Only for Out-of-Training Knowledge: A Controlled Study on Clinical Question Answering
arxiv-2606-22419.creator: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

pmc-10633864.title: QSPR Analysis of Drugs for Treatment of Schizophrenia Using Topological Indices
pmc-10633864.creator: Xiujun Zhang, Muhammad Jawwad Saif, Nazeran Idrees, Salma Kanwal, Saima Parveen, Fatima Saeed
pmc-10633864.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized primarily by cognitive deficits. Drugs and therapies are helpful in managing the symptoms, mostly with long-term compliance. There is a pressing need to design more efficient drugs with fewer adverse effects. Solubility, metabolic stability, toxicity, permeability, and transporter effects are important parameters in the efficacy of drug design, which in turn depend upon different physical and chemical characteristics of drugs.

pmc-11344459.title: Screening and molecular docking verification of feature genes related to phospholipid metabolism in hepatocarcinoma caused by hepatitis B
pmc-11344459.creator: Jian Zhang, Fengmei Zhang, Lei Zhang, Meiling Zhang, Shuye Liu, Ying Ma
pmc-11344459.description: BackgroundThe progression of tumours is related to abnormal phospholipid metabolism. This study is anticipated to present a fresh perspective for disease therapy targets of hepatocarcinoma caused by hepatitis B virus in the future by screening feature genes related to phospholipid metabolism.MethodsThis study analysed GSE121248 to pinpoint differentially expressed genes (DEGs).

pmc-11511554.title: Effective Acoustic Model-Based Beamforming Training for Static and Dynamic Hri Applications
pmc-11511554.creator: Alejandro Luzanto, Nicolás Bohmer, Rodrigo Mahu, Eduardo Alvarado, Richard M Stern, Néstor Becerra Yoma, Nader Jalili, Soroush Korivand
pmc-11511554.description: Human–robot collaboration will play an important role in the fourth industrial revolution in applications related to hostile environments, mining, industry, forestry, education, natural disaster and defense. Effective collaboration requires robots to understand human intentions and tasks, which involves advanced user profiling. Voice-based communication, rich in complex information, is key to this.

pmc-11533558.title: Early prediction of cognitive impairment in adults aged 20 years and older using machine learning and biomarkers of heavy metal exposure
pmc-11533558.creator: Ali Nabavi, Farimah Safari, Mohammad Kashkooli, Sara Sadat Nabavizadeh, Hossein Molavi Vardanjani
pmc-11533558.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Cognitive impairment, Heavy metal exposure, Predictive models Introduction The rising prevalence of cognitive dysfunction presents a significant challenge to modern healthcare systems worldwide. As the global population ages, conditions characterized by cognitive impairment, such as dementia, are expected to impact an ever-increasing number of individuals (Crimmins et al., 2011, Ngandu et al., 2015).

pmc-11641688.title: Functions of TAM Receptors and Ligands Protein S and Gas6 in Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Disease
pmc-11641688.creator: Teagan Prouse, Samarpan Majumder, Rinku Majumder
pmc-11641688.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease are associated with high morbidity and mortality in industrialized nations. The Tyro3, Axl, and Mer (TAM) family of receptor tyrosine kinases is involved in the amplification or resolution of atherosclerosis pathology and other cardiovascular pathology. The ligands of these receptors, Protein S (PS) and growth arrest specific protein 6 (Gas6), are essential for TAM receptor functions in the amplification and resolution of atherosclerosis. The Axl-Gas6 interaction has various effects on cardiovascular disease.

pmc-11699072.title: Catalytic degradation of aromatic dyes using triazolidine-thione stabilized nickel nanoparticles
pmc-11699072.creator: Shahnaz, Attiya-E Rasool, Warda Parveen
pmc-11699072.description: Nanoparticles have been extensively studied for many years due to their important roles in catalysis, metallurgy and high temperature superconductors. But, Nanoparticles are extremely unstable and easily react with other substances. So, to control the size and the shape of nanoparticles they must be stabilized. Organic Ligands have gain more attention for stabilizing Nanoparticles.

pmc-12644378.title: Contrast-enhanced mammography-guided biopsy: principles, challenges, and opportunities
pmc-12644378.creator: Rodrigo Alcantara, Javier Azcona, Mireia Pitarch, Elisenda Vall, Elisabet Vila-Trias, E. Natalia Arenas
pmc-12644378.description: Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM)-guided biopsy enables the tissue sampling of enhancing breast lesions that are not visible on conventional imaging. The technique combines dual-energy stereotactic acquisition with intravenous contrast administration, allowing accurate targeting of recombined-only lesions. It represents a practical alternative to MRI-guided biopsy, particularly in settings where MRI access is limited or contraindicated.

pmc-12659141.title: Personalized models of eating disorder symptoms and suicide risk in anorexia nervosa spectrum disorders: protocol for a longitudinal, passive-sensing study
pmc-12659141.creator: Lauren M. Harris, Rachel Torres, Elizabeth D. Cash, April R. Smith, Cheri A. Levinson
pmc-12659141.description: BackgroundIndividuals with Anorexia Nervosa and Atypical Anorexia (termed here Anorexia Nervosa Spectrum Disorder, or ANSD) are at elevated suicide risk, yet limited research has explored the progression from suicidal ideation to suicide attempts among individuals with ANSD. Leveraging intensive real-time data, the present study will identify the behavioral, physiological, and psychological mechanisms linking ANSD and suicide.

pmc-12690537.title: First person – Roza Masalmeh
pmc-12690537.creator: Unknown
pmc-12690537.description: First Person is a series of interviews with the first authors of a selection of papers published in Disease Models & Mechanisms, helping researchers promote themselves alongside their papers. Roza Masalmeh is first author on ‘ FAK modulates glioblastoma stem cell energetics via regulation of glycolysis and glutamine oxidation’, published in DMM.

pmc-12746098.title: 3D enhancer architecture coordinated by CTCF determines immune-related gene expression patterns via RNA polymerase II pause-release in CD4+ T cells
pmc-12746098.creator: Eun-Chong Lee, Kyungwoo Kim, Sugyung Kim, Mikyoung Kim, Hyoung-Pyo Kim
pmc-12746098.description: CTCF (CCCTC-binding factor) is crucial for organizing mammalian genomes into domains and structural loops, yet its role in enhancer–promoter interactions remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that 3D enhancer architecture undergoes marked reorganization upon CTCF depletion in activated CD4+ T cells. Despite this, active transcription, particularly driven by STAT5-bound super-enhancers, maintains enhancer loops independently of CTCF.

pmc-13082252.title: How Key in vivo Models Can Advance Anticancer Nanotherapeutics
pmc-13082252.creator: Gudapureddy Radha, B Devika Chithrani
pmc-13082252.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nanomedicine offers powerful opportunities for targeted drug delivery and cancer therapy, yet clinical translation remains limited by the complex and dynamic interactions of nanoparticles within biological systems. This review integrates current evidence on how nanoparticle size, shape, and surface properties govern cellular uptake and processing, systemic biodistribution, immune interactions, and therapeutic performance across in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo models.

pmc-13242799.title: Efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Combined with Exercise in Patients with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis [Response to Letter]
pmc-13242799.creator: Yi-Zhao Zhang, Biao Yang, Cheng-Hao Jiang, Yu-Xuan Guo, Xin-Xin Lai, Wei-Qiang Zhang, He Zhang
pmc-13242799.description: e, we stated that “shared control groups were split proportionally”; however, more precise wording would have been that “shared arms were split proportionally”. In multi-arm trials, the arm requiring adjustment is the shared arm, which may be either the intervention arm or the comparator arm, depending on the specific analytic contrast.

pmc-13284551.title: Changes in Functional Brain Activity in School-Age Children 10 Years Later: A Resting State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study
pmc-13284551.creator: Lin Li, Yanshu Ding, Lihan Chen, Fei Liu, Yunzhi Ling, Renzhang Lin, Wanchao Zhang, Kaihua Jiang
pmc-13284551.description: Objective Children’s cognitive function is undergoing great dynamic changes with age. This study aims to explore the characteristics of changes in children’s cognitive function before and after 10 years, and discover brain areas where brain function has undergone significant changes.

pmc-13631292.title: CRACD loss drives hypoxia-induced immune escape in gastric cancer
pmc-13631292.creator: Yoojeong Seo, Jinho Jang, Kyung-Pil Ko, Gengyi Zou, Sang-Min Kim, Yuanjian Huang, Shengzhe Zhang, Jie Zhang, Sohee Jun, Wonhong Chu, Vishwa Venkatesan, Sanjana Dhakshinamoorthy, Hyunki Kim, Jae-Il Park
pmc-13631292.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mucinous gastric adenocarcinoma (MGC) is a distinct histologic subtype characterized by poor prognosis and limited responsiveness to chemotherapy and immunotherapy. CRACD, an actin polymerization regulator, is frequently inactivated in gastric cancer (GC), with enrichment in mucinous subtypes. We found that genetic engineering of murine gastric organoids with Cracd ablation combined with Kras mutation and Trp53 loss induced mucinous cell plasticity, disrupted epithelial integrity, and promoted immune evasion.
